title: Archidocs model file (any other *.yaml in a Project)

people.description: Persons, keyed by id. An id is unique in the Project across all its Elements and Deployment Targets.

systems.description: Systems, keyed by id, each with its Services nested under `services`.

services.description: Services declared at the top level, keyed by id: those outside any System, and those that join a System with `in`.

components.description: Components declared at the top level, keyed by id. Each names its Service with `in`.

targets.description: Deployment Targets, keyed by id and nested as they nest. Their ids share the Project's ids with its Elements.

deployments.description: Deployments: which Service runs in which Environment on which Deployment Target, with its URLs.

service.description: The Service that runs: an id in this Project, or `project:id`. It must name a Service, not a System or a Component.

environment.description: The Environment it runs in: the id of an Environment in `workspace.yaml`.

target.description: The Deployment Target it runs on: an id in this Project, or `project:id` for one another Project declares.

url.description: The Service's main URL in this Environment. A full URL, such as `https://cart.example.com`.

endpoints.description: Further named URLs of the Service in this Environment, such as a health check or an admin console.

name.description: What the endpoint is, such as `health` or `admin`.

url.description: The endpoint's address. A full URL.

items.description: A further named URL of the Service in this Environment.

anyOf.description: A fixed number of instances, such as `3`.

min.description: The fewest instances the autoscaler runs.

max.description: The most instances the autoscaler runs. At least `min`.

anyOf.description: An autoscale range, such as `{ min: 2, max: 10 }`.

instances.description: How many interchangeable copies of the Service run on this Deployment Target: a whole number for a fixed count, such as `3`, or `{ min, max }` for an autoscale range, such as `{ min: 2, max: 10 }`. Use it for identical workers on one Target, such as an App Service plan running N instances. When where each copy runs matters, such as one per availability zone or VM, declare separate Deployments on separate Targets instead. Default: 1.

items.description: A Deployment: one Service running in one Environment on one Deployment Target. The three together name it, so the same three can appear only once.

structural.description: Structural Views and Deployment Views, keyed by id. Other Projects name a View as `project:id`.

description.description: What the View shows, or the question it answers.

level.description: The level every selected Element is collapsed to. `c1`: Persons and Systems. `c2`: Services, grouped in their Systems. `c3`: Components, inside their Services. `deployment`: a Deployment View, which places Deployments on their Deployment Targets in one Environment and needs `environment`.

expand.description: Elements to open one level deeper than `level`, showing their children. Each is an id in this Project, or `project:id`, and must be a node of the View that has children. A Deployment View ignores it.

items.description: An id in this Project, or `project:id` for one in another Project.

collapse.description: Elements to close, hiding everything inside them. Each is an id in this Project, or `project:id`, and must be a node of the View that has children. A Deployment View ignores it.

items.description: An id in this Project, or `project:id` for one in another Project.

direction.description: The way the diagram runs. `TB`: top to bottom. `BT`: bottom to top. `LR`: left to right. `RL`: right to left. Default: `LR`, or `TB` for a Deployment View.

environment.description: For a Deployment View (`level: deployment`), which must have it, and for no other View: the Environment shown, as the id of an Environment in `workspace.yaml`.

targets.description: For a Deployment View (`level: deployment`) only: shows only the Deployments on these Deployment Targets and on the Targets inside them. Each is an id in this Project, or `project:id`. Default: every Deployment Target.

items.description: An id in this Project, or `project:id` for one in another Project.

include.description: Selectors for the Elements to show. Default: every Element in the Workspace.

exclude.description: Selectors for the Elements to leave out of what `include` picked. An excluded Element takes everything inside it with it.

additionalProperties.description: A structural Saved View: the Elements its selectors pick, drawn at one `level`. With `level: deployment` it is a Deployment View. Its key is the View's id, unique among the Project's Saved Views.

dynamic.description: Dynamic Views, keyed by id. Other Projects name a View as `project:id`.

participants.description: Elements that take part, in the order to draw them, each as an id in this Project or `project:id`. Participants not listed follow, in the order the Steps first use them. An Element and its own ancestor can't both take part. Default: the order the Steps first use them.

items.description: An id in this Project, or `project:id` for one in another Project.

from.description: The Element the Step starts at: the consumer of a call, the Publisher of an event, or the sender of a reply. An id in this Project, or `project:id`.

to.description: The Element the Step reaches: the provider of a call, the Subscriber of an event, or the receiver of a reply. An id in this Project, or `project:id`.

relationship.description: The `id` of the Relationship the Step takes, as an id in this Project or `project:id`. Needed only when several Relationships match the two Elements.

description.description: The text on the Step's arrow. Default: the Relationship's `description`, or its `channel` for an event.

note.description: A note shown under the Step.

return.description: `true` makes the Step the reply to a sync Relationship declared from `to` to `from`. An async Relationship has no reply. Default: `false`.

items.description: A Step: one interaction of the scenario, which must follow a Relationship in the Model. It is a call from a consumer to its provider, an event from a Publisher to a Subscriber, or with `return: true` a reply.

steps.description: The Steps of the scenario, in order.

additionalProperties.description: A Dynamic View: one scenario as an ordered list of Steps, shown as a sequence chart. Its key is the View's id, unique among the Project's Saved Views.

views.description: The Project's Saved Views: `structural` ones, which include Deployment Views, and `dynamic` ones.

description: A Project file: any `.yaml` file in a Project folder other than `project.yaml`.

description.description: What the Element is or does, in a sentence or two.

owner.description: The Team that owns the Element: the id of a Team in `workspace.yaml`. Set it only when it differs from the Project's; nothing is inherited from the parent Element. Default: the Project's `owner`.

tags.description: Free-form labels. A Saved View's `{tag}` selector picks Elements by them.

links.description: Links to pages about the Element, such as a runbook or a dashboard.

metadata.description: Free-form facts about the Element that the Model has no field for, such as `tier: 1` or `on-call: payments-oncall`. Keys are labels, shown as written; values are strings, numbers or booleans. Nothing in the Model reads them: they are shown in the viewer and returned by the MCP server.

relationships.description: The Relationships this Element is the consumer of: what it depends on. A Relationship is never declared under its provider.

Person.title: Person
Person.description: A Person: a human or role that uses a System, such as a shopper or a support agent. A Person is only ever the consumer in a Relationship.

label.description: The text of the link, such as `Runbook`.

url.description: The page the link opens. A full URL, such as `https://wiki.example.com/runbooks/web`.

Link.title: Link
Link.description: A link to a page about the thing it is declared on, such as a runbook or a dashboard.

to.description: The provider: the Element this one depends on. An id in this Project, or `project:id` for an Element in another Project. It can't be a Person, this Element itself, or an ancestor or descendant of this Element.

id.description: An id for the Relationship, unique among the Project's Relationships. Needed only when several Relationships connect the same two Elements, so that a Dynamic View Step can name one.

description.description: What the consumer uses the provider for, as a verb phrase that reads from consumer to provider, such as `Reads prices from`.

technology.description: How the consumer reaches the provider: a protocol, a driver or a format, such as `JSON/HTTPS`, `gRPC` or `SQL`.

interaction.description: `sync`: a call that waits for an answer. `async`: an event or message that gets no reply, such as an event through a broker or a webhook. Default: `sync`.

via.description: For an `async` Relationship only: the broker the events travel through. A Service with `type: broker`, as an id in this Project or `project:id`. Leave it out when there is no broker, as with a webhook.

channel.description: For an `async` Relationship only: the topic or queue the events travel on, such as `orders.placed`.

Relationship.title: Relationship
Relationship.description: A Relationship: a dependency of the Element it is declared under (the consumer) on the Element `to` names (the provider). Declare it once, under the consumer.

description.description: What the Element is or does, in a sentence or two.

owner.description: The Team that owns the Element: the id of a Team in `workspace.yaml`. Set it only when it differs from the Project's; nothing is inherited from the parent Element. Default: the Project's `owner`.

tags.description: Free-form labels. A Saved View's `{tag}` selector picks Elements by them.

links.description: Links to pages about the Element, such as a runbook or a dashboard.

metadata.description: Free-form facts about the Element that the Model has no field for, such as `tier: 1` or `on-call: payments-oncall`. Keys are labels, shown as written; values are strings, numbers or booleans. Nothing in the Model reads them: they are shown in the viewer and returned by the MCP server.

relationships.description: The Relationships this Element is the consumer of: what it depends on. A Relationship is never declared under its provider.

external.description: `true` for a System run outside the organization, such as a payment provider. Nothing inside an External System can declare Components. Default: `false`.

repository.description: The full URL of the source code repository the Element is built from. Shown as a link in the viewer.

services.description: The Services in the System, keyed by id.

System.title: System
System.description: A System: a named grouping of Services that together deliver a business capability. Systems do not nest.

description.description: What the Element is or does, in a sentence or two.

owner.description: The Team that owns the Element: the id of a Team in `workspace.yaml`. Set it only when it differs from the Project's; nothing is inherited from the parent Element. Default: the Project's `owner`.

tags.description: Free-form labels. A Saved View's `{tag}` selector picks Elements by them.

links.description: Links to pages about the Element, such as a runbook or a dashboard.

metadata.description: Free-form facts about the Element that the Model has no field for, such as `tier: 1` or `on-call: payments-oncall`. Keys are labels, shown as written; values are strings, numbers or booleans. Nothing in the Model reads them: they are shown in the viewer and returned by the MCP server.

relationships.description: The Relationships this Element is the consumer of: what it depends on. A Relationship is never declared under its provider.

type.description: What the Service is; each type is drawn differently. `app`: an application, the usual case. `datastore`: a database or other store. `broker`: a message broker that async Relationships run through, named by their `via`. Default: `app`.

technology.description: What the Service is built with, such as `Go` or `PostgreSQL`. Shown under its name.

repository.description: The full URL of the source code repository the Element is built from. Shown as a link in the viewer.

external.description: `true` for a Service run outside the organization, such as a payment provider's API. An External Service can't declare Components. Default: `false`.

in.description: The System this Service belongs to, as an id in this Project. Only for a Service under the top-level `services` key, and not allowed for one nested under a System's `services`. Without it, a top-level Service stands outside any System.

components.description: The Components inside the Service, keyed by id.

Service.title: Service
Service.description: A Service: a deployable, addressable unit of software; the thing that has a URL and a Deployment.

description.description: What the Element is or does, in a sentence or two.

owner.description: The Team that owns the Element: the id of a Team in `workspace.yaml`. Set it only when it differs from the Project's; nothing is inherited from the parent Element. Default: the Project's `owner`.

tags.description: Free-form labels. A Saved View's `{tag}` selector picks Elements by them.

links.description: Links to pages about the Element, such as a runbook or a dashboard.

metadata.description: Free-form facts about the Element that the Model has no field for, such as `tier: 1` or `on-call: payments-oncall`. Keys are labels, shown as written; values are strings, numbers or booleans. Nothing in the Model reads them: they are shown in the viewer and returned by the MCP server.

relationships.description: The Relationships this Element is the consumer of: what it depends on. A Relationship is never declared under its provider.

technology.description: What the Component is built with, such as `TypeScript module`. Shown under its name.

repository.description: The full URL of the source code repository the Element is built from. Shown as a link in the viewer.

in.description: The Service this Component belongs to, as an id in this Project. Required for a Component under the top-level `components` key, and not allowed for one nested under a Service's `components`.

Component.title: Component
Component.description: A Component: a part inside a Service that is not deployed on its own.

kind.description: What the Deployment Target is, in a short word you choose, printed as written in its header: prefer short forms such as `region`, `az`, `vnet`, `snet`, `vm`, `aks`, `ns` or `asp` over long names like `availability-zone` or `subnet`.

description.description: What the Deployment Target is, in a sentence or two.

owner.description: The Team that owns the Deployment Target: the id of a Team in `workspace.yaml`. Default: the Project's `owner`.

tags.description: Free-form labels for the Deployment Target.

links.description: Links to pages about the Deployment Target, such as a dashboard.

targets.description: The Deployment Targets inside this one, keyed by id, such as the clusters in a region.

Target.title: Deployment Target
Target.description: A Deployment Target: a place Services run, such as a region, a cluster in it or a platform. Deployment Targets nest to any depth and are not Elements.

anyOf.description: One Element, by its id: an id in this Project, or `project:id`.

element.description: The Element to start from: an id in this Project, or `project:id`.

with.description: Also selects what is inside the Element. `children`: the Elements directly inside it. `descendants`: everything inside it, at any depth.

upstream.description: Also selects the Elements upstream of it, those that depend on it: a number of hops, or `all` for every one of them.

downstream.description: Also selects the Elements downstream of it, those it depends on: a number of hops, or `all` for every one of them.

anyOf.description: One Element, and optionally what is inside it and what is upstream or downstream of it.

team.description: The Team: the id of a Team in `workspace.yaml`.

tag.description: The tag, as written in the Elements' `tags`.

anyOf.description: Every Element that carries a tag.

Selector.title: Selector
Selector.description: One entry of a Saved View's `include` or `exclude`: an id, or a map that picks several Elements at once.

from.description: One end of the paths: an id in this Project, or `project:id`.

to.description: The other end of the paths: an id in this Project, or `project:id`.

paths.description: Which paths to take. `shortest`: the shortest paths, however long. A number n: every path of at most n hops. Default: `shortest`.

PathSelector.title: Path selector
PathSelector.description: The paths between two Elements, followed in both directions. As a selector it picks every Element on them; as a Lens it highlights them.

impact.description: The Element whose impact is highlighted: an id in this Project, or `project:id`.

direction.description: Which side to highlight. `upstream`: what depends on the Element. `downstream`: what it depends on. `both`: both sides. Default: `both`.

anyOf.description: The Impact Lens: what is upstream or downstream of one Element, each node marked with how many hops away it is.

team.description: The Team: the id of a Team in `workspace.yaml`.

anyOf.description: The Team Lens: what one Team owns.
The Path Lens: the paths between two Elements.

Lens.title: Lens
Lens.description: The Lens the View opens with. A Lens highlights nodes and never changes which nodes the View shows.
